newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-START OF WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL DELAYED.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-START OF WOMEN'S WORLD CUP DOWNHILL DELAYED.

text.p: The start of a women's Alpine skiing World Cup downhill on Friday was delayed by an hour due to heavy snowfall at the Austrian resort.

Organisers said the start of the season's third downhill had been put back from 1200 local time (1100 GMT) to 1300 (1200 GMT) to give workers more time to prepare the 3,010-metre long Strohsack piste.
But the organisers insisted the course was in excellent condition and the race would go ahead on Friday despite continuing snowfall.

Friday's race is the replacement for a downhill which had to be called off in Crans Montana, Switzerland, in December. Bad Kleinkirchheim is due to host a second downhill on Saturday and a super-giant slalom on Sunday.
A training run on Wednesday had to be called off because warm temperatures had softened the piste, which then had to be treated with a chemical which hardens snow.
